rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~96%, half point priced out (CME FedWatch via Reuters, Hercules, Nov 23); ECB Dec ~90%; BoE Dec ~80%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoC Dec ~44%; RBA 4.85%
rows.read: A quarter-point December Fed hike is still treated as all but certain, even after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned against hiking too far. The European Central Bank, Bank of England and Bank of Japan are all expected to hike in December as well.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Germany composite PMI Nov 55.0; France 46.2; euro area 51.7; UK 52.3, services 52.0; Australia composite 46.1; Chicago Fed activity index Oct −0.06
rows.read: Germany's economy sped up in November while France's shrank faster, early surveys showed, and UK services growth slowed. Australian firms are cutting output and jobs. A Chicago Fed gauge put US activity slightly below trend in October.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US core PCE Oct due Wed (fcst +0.3% m/m, 3.2% y/y); UK CPI Oct 3.6%, core 2.8%; euro-area CPI Oct 4.0%; Australia CPI Oct due Tue (fcst 4.8% y/y)
rows.read: Inflation is still well above target almost everywhere, which keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes. Australian firms say price rises are slowing, which eases pressure on their central bank. Wednesday's US core inflation figures are the big test for the Fed this week.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: US 2-year ~4.76% (Friday 4.63%); USD/JPY ~159.08 (+0.36%); USD/CHF ~0.8387; STOXX 600 recovering after a nearly 6% weekly fall
rows.read: Stocks steadied after last week's slide in technology shares, and European shares won back some of their losses. That cooled demand for the yen and lifted US yields. Iran's promise to fight the US naval blockade keeps some caution alive.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar after betting on it, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US 10-year ~5.04% (Friday 4.92%); France composite PMI 46.2, a six-month low; ECB Financial Stability Review: France debt 119% of GDP, deficit 5.5%
rows.read: France's debts, flagged by the European Central Bank as a risk, weigh more now that its economy looks close to recession. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs high, with the 10-year yield back above 5%.
